governing_question: What would it take for an Arkansas household to become more secure, more solvent, more asset-owning, less exposed to unavoidable costs, and richer in both money and time?
central_proposition: Prosperity is not merely earning more. It is retaining more, owning more, becoming less fragile, gaining greater agency, and having more control over one's time.
organizing_sentence: Constitutional Capitalism succeeds only when Arkansas households improve across income, cost, security, ownership, and discretionary time — measured against Arkansas NOW, not against GDP slogans.

dimensions.label: Income
dimensions.definition: How much enters the household (earned, benefits, ownership income, applicable transfers).

dimensions.label: Cost
dimensions.definition: How much must leave just to participate in society (essentials + required obligations).

dimensions.label: Security
dimensions.definition: How vulnerable the household is to disruption (shocks, buffers, insurance, cliffs).

dimensions.label: Ownership
dimensions.definition: How much of today's economic activity becomes tomorrow's household capital.

dimensions.label: Time
dimensions.definition: How much life remains after earning income and meeting obligations — discretionary time as a prosperity dimension.

five_dimension_framework.insight: Conventional discussion collapses these into wages or GDP. Constitutional Capitalism refuses that collapse.

sections.title: The Household as the Unit of Success
body: GDP, state revenue, job counts, and median wages are necessary context — and insufficient success tests.
A state can grow output while households lose surplus, security, ownership, and time.
Pass 3.1 Arkansas NOW supplies the inherited baseline; Pass 3.2 defines what improvement means for the unit that must feel it: the household.
insufficient_alone: Median wage without cost, security, ownership, and time
sections.success_test: CC succeeds only if households retain more usable surplus, greater security, and greater ownership over time

sections.title: Household Prosperity Surplus
sections.time_dimension: Discretionary time remains a separate prosperity dimension — not reducible to money.
sections.insight: A household earning $80k while spending $78k to maintain basic social participation is not necessarily more prosperous than one earning $65k with dramatically lower unavoidable costs and greater asset ownership.
sections.mathematical_validation: DEFERRED_STAGE_4 — architecture complete; no fabricated statewide surplus figure

sections.title: NOW → FUTURE Household Transition
sections.rule: Improve households without abolish-today. Dependency Rule from Transition Engine binds.

engine_transmission.path: Income/capital retention → household resources line; ownership ladders → ownership income
Capability → earning power + entrepreneurship + civic capacity (unabridged in 3.3)
Taxes, services, rights, regulation, transfers — Public Dollar Chain judged by household effect
Food/energy/housing/healthcare infrastructure alter essential costs — sector depth in 3.6
Sequenced bridges; no sudden removal of inherited supports households still need

sections.prosperity_loop: Arkansas earns/retains capital → productive ownership generates value → value reaches households → essential costs controlled/reduced → household surplus increases → households acquire assets → Arkansas capital base grows → Money Engine strengthens
sections.extraction_loop: Capital leakage → weak ownership → lower household capture → high unavoidable costs → little surplus → little asset formation → dependency/external ownership → greater leakage

pressure_stack.title: Arkansas Household Pressure Stack
pressure_stack.reverse_insight: Multiple modest structural improvements can compound at the household level — more convincing than one giant program.
pressure_stack.policy_implication: Household policy cannot be siloed. Cost domains interact through time, access, and risk.

counterarguments.claim: Lowering essential costs will suppress market supply.
counterarguments.strong_form: Price ceilings or heavy subsidy can shrink housing, care, or energy supply and worsen shortages.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: CC prefers ownership, competition, supply expansion, and anti-extraction before crude price suppression. Dependency Rule forbids abolish-today of existing capacity.
counterarguments.unresolved: STAGE_4 incidence and supply-elasticity tests by sector (often via 3.6 joins).

counterarguments.claim: Public intervention crowds out private provision.
counterarguments.strong_form: State entry displaces private providers and reduces innovation.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Government role is capacity, rules, and public return where markets fail — not universal state landlord or sole employer. Markets remain primary in most household goods.

counterarguments.claim: Supports create dependency and destroy work incentives.
counterarguments.strong_form: Transfers without work requirements trap households and shrink labor supply.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Surplus architecture targets productive participation, ownership, and cliff reduction. Care is treated as economic infrastructure enabling work — not as indefinite consumption.

counterarguments.strong_form: Standardized public models erase household preference diversity.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Archetypes exist precisely because preferences and geographies differ. Portable supports and ownership pathways preserve choice within anti-extraction rules.
counterarguments.unresolved: Design detail in 3.5/3.6 — not a reason to abandon household metrics.

counterarguments.claim: Disposable income gains just inflate scarce goods like housing.
counterarguments.strong_form: Income transfers capitalize into rents/prices, leaving surplus unchanged.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Pressure Stack requires simultaneous cost-side and ownership-side reforms. Income-only policy is rejected by the five-dimension framework.
counterarguments.unresolved: STAGE_4 capitalization tests; housing supply in 3.6.

counterarguments.claim: Subsidized consumption is not real prosperity.
counterarguments.strong_form: If surplus is manufactured by transfers, households are not more capable or independent.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: True prosperity requires surplus that can become security, savings, ownership, capability, and time — not perpetual subsidy as the end state.
counterarguments.unresolved: Measurement must separate temporary bridges from durable capital formation (Stage 4).

counterarguments.strong_form: Household cost relief expands deficits without replacement revenue.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: COUNTABLE engines remain $0 until Stage 4 clears. Money Engine + Dependency Rule forbid pretending. Household chapter does not invent revenue.

counterarguments.claim: Personal responsibility, savings, work, and market discipline are ignored.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Agency is inside prosperity: surplus uses ladder includes savings, ownership, entrepreneurship, and time. Structure shapes the feasible set; it does not abolish responsibility.
counterarguments.unresolved: Behavioral response estimation Stage 4 — not a substitute for cost/ownership architecture.
